questions.text:
The weights of kiwifruit from a packhouse in Te Puke are normally distributed with a mean of 95 g and a standard deviation of 12 g.

(i) Find the probability that a randomly selected kiwifruit weighs more than 105 g.
(ii) Find the probability that a randomly selected kiwifruit weighs between 80 g and 110 g.

An exporter wants to sell bags of kiwifruit that contain the heaviest 80% of kiwifruit from this orchard.

(i) Find the minimum weight of kiwifruit that would be included in these bags.
(ii) What percentage of kiwifruit would be rejected (too light) for the bags?
questions.markingGuide:
Step 1: Merit: (i) Bottom 20% excluded.

Step 2: z for 20th percentile = -0.842.

Step 3: Weight = 95 + (-0.842)(12) = 95 - 10.1 = 84.9 g.

Step 4: Kiwifruit must weigh at least 84.9 g.

Step 5: (ii) 20% of kiwifruit would be rejected.

questions.text:
A shuttle departs every 15 minutes from the wharf. The waiting time for a passenger who arrives at random follows a uniform distribution on the interval [0, 15] minutes.

(i) Write down the probability density function for the waiting time.
(ii) Find the expected waiting time and the standard deviation of the waiting time.
(iii) Find the probability that a passenger waits more than 10 minutes.
questions.markingGuide:
Step 1: Achievement: (i) f(x) = 1/15 for 0 ≤ x ≤ 15, f(x) = 0 otherwise.

Step 2: (ii) E(X) = (0 + 15)/2 = 7.5 minutes.

Step 3: SD = (15 - 0)/√12 = 15/3.464 = 4.33 minutes.

Step 4: (iii) P(X > 10) = (15 - 10)/15 = 5/15 = 1/3.

questions.text:
The time between significant earthquakes of a certain magnitude in the Taupō Volcanic Zone can be modelled by an exponential distribution with a mean of 30 years.

(i) Find the probability that the next eruption of this magnitude occurs within 20 years.
(ii) Given that 20 years have already passed without such an eruption, find the probability of waiting at least another 20 years.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- (i) λ = 1/30.
- P(X ≤ 20) = 1 - e^(-20/30) = 1 - e^(-0.667) = 1 - 0.5134 = 0.4866.

For Merit:
- (ii) By the memoryless property of the exponential distribution, P(X > 40 | X > 20) = P(X > 20) = e^(-20/30) = e^(-0.667) = 0.5134.
- The probability of waiting another 20 years is the same regardless of how long we've already waited.
- This is the key property of the exponential distribution.

questions.text:
The random variable X has the probability density function:

f(x) = kx(8 - x) for 0 ≤ x ≤ 6
f(x) = 0 otherwise

(i) Find the value of k.
(ii) Find E(X).
(iii) Find P(X > 4).

The volume of milk in bottles is normally distributed with a mean of 510 mL and a standard deviation of 8 mL. Bottles are labelled as containing 500 mL of milk.

(i) Find the probability that a randomly selected bottle contains less than the labelled volume.
(ii) The manufacturer wants no more than 2% of bottles to be underfilled. To what value should the mean volume be set, assuming the standard deviation stays at 8 mL?
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Merit:
- (i) z = (500 - 510)/8 = -1.25.
- P(Z < -1.25) = 0.1056 ≈ 10.6%.

For Excellence:
- (ii) Need P(X < 500) ≤ 0.02.
- z for 2% tail = -2.054.
- 500 = μ + (-2.054)(8).
- μ = 500 + 2.054 × 8 = 500 + 16.43 = 516.4 mL.
- The mean should be set to at least 516.4 mL.
